[[Jesuit High School (Sacramento)|Jesuit]] ([[Sacramento, California]]) | college = [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]] (2008–2012) | draft_year = 2012 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 30 | draft_team = [[Golden State Warriors]] | career_start = 2012 | career_end = 2016; 2021 | career_position = [[Center (basketball)|Center]] | career_number = 31, 20 | years1 = {{nbay|2012|start}}–{{nbay|2015|end}} | team1 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | years2 = 2015 | team2 = →[[Santa Cruz Warriors]] | years3 = [[2020–21 NBA G League season|2021]] | team3 = [[Westchester Knicks]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] ([[2015 NBA Finals|2015]]) * Second-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2011) }} '''Ifeanyi Festus Ezeli-Ndulue''' {{Audio|LL-Q33578 (ibo)-Obefelix-Ifeanyi Festus.wav|Listen|help=no}}(born October 21, 1989) is a Nigerian-American former professional [[basketball]] player who played five seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt Commodores]] before being selected with the 30th overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]] by the [[Golden State Warriors]], where he won an [[2015 NBA Finals|NBA Championship]] in 2015. Ezeli last appeared in the [[2016 NBA Finals]] and did not play basketball due to knee surgery in the 2017 season, then coming back in 2021. ==Early life== ===Life in Nigeria=== One of five children, Ezeli remembered in a 2011 interview with [[Andy Katz]] of [[ESPN.com]], "My parents told me I was an unusual child. My first name is Ifeanyi, and that means 'nothing is impossible with God'. That sets the tone for my journey while I'm alive."{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/blog/_/name/katz_andy/id/684764 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201027031950/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/blog/_/name/katz_andy/id/684764 |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 27, 2020 |title=Festus Ezeli continues to learn the game |first=Andy |last=Katz |publisher=ESPN |date=August 9, 2011 |access-date=October 24, 2020}} Ezeli concentrated on academics, graduating from high school when he was only 14, and aspiring to become a physician. To further his career goals, Ezeli's parents sent him to live with his uncle, a [[pediatrician]], in [[Yuba City, California]] in 2004.{{cite web|url= http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1182629/index.htm |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110304225533/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1182629/index.htm |url-status= dead |archive-date= March 4, 2011 |title=How Did I Get Here? |first=Pablo S. |last=Torre |work=Sports Illustrated |date=March 7, 2011 |access-date=August 15, 2011}} ===Life in America=== Shortly after Ezeli arrived in Yuba City, his uncle encouraged him to take up what seemed to be the most appropriate sport for a {{convert|6|ft|8|in|m|adj=on}} teenager—basketball. This proved much more difficult for Ezeli than academics because he had never played any organized sports despite the fact that Ezeli played soccer as a child.{{cite web|url=http://www.secdigitalnetwork.com/SECNation/BlueRibbon/tabid/1502/Article/222196/one-on-one-with-chris-dortch-festus-ezeli.aspx |title=One-On-One With Chris Dortch: Festus Ezeli |first=Chris |last=Dortch |work=Blue Ribbon Basketball Yearbook |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=March 10, 2011 |access-date=August 15, 2011}} He took a year of classes at [[Jesuit High School (Sacramento)|Jesuit High School]] in [[Sacramento]] but did not play basketball; different sources report that Ezeli was either ineligible to play because he had graduated from high school in Nigeria or cut during tryouts. The start of Ezeli's organized basketball career, with a low-level [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] team, was especially inauspicious since his first points were scored in his own team's basket. Recalling that incident, Ezeli said, "Everybody was running up the court, and I was just running with them. It's kind of surreal. Sometimes I think about it now and I'm like, Damn. How did I get here?" Also in the Katz interview, Ezeli remarked on his struggles to learn the game:
"I didn't know what I was doing. Imagine someone who is 14 or 15 years old, and you're teaching them as if they're a 6-year-old. It was tough. Everyone was getting frustrated with me. I was getting frustrated with it. I tried playing in 2005. I stopped. I tried again in 2006. And when I had my first dunk in a summer league game in Las Vegas in 2006, that's when I was so excited. It was so exhilarating that I started to like it."
At age 16, Ezeli joined a second AAU team and also enrolled part-time at [[Yuba Community College]]. By not attending full-time, he retained a full four years of college eligibility and was still able to practice with the team; Ezeli also served as the team's [[videography|videographer]]. Although still learning the most basic of basketball skills, Ezeli made his high-level competitive debut on the AAU circuit in the summer of 2007.{{cite web|url=http://nashvillecitypaper.com/content/sports/big-man-finally-positioned-play-big-role-vanderbilt-basketball |title=Big man finally positioned to play big role for Vanderbilt basketball |first=Jerome |last=Boettcher |work=Nashville City Paper |date=November 11, 2010 |access-date=August 15, 2011}} By then, Ezeli had reached {{convert|6|ft|11|in}}, and averaged 10 points, 11 rebounds, and three blocks per game, earning an invitation to the Reebok All-American Camp in July 2007. ===Recruitment=== Ezeli's appearance at the camp marked a major turning point in his life. According to ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' writer [[Pablo Torre (journalist)|Pablo Torre]],
"Recruiters...awaited his arrival as if he were [[Bigfoot]]. They left with their heads spinning at Ezeli's size and raw potential, even if it was clear that he lacked confidence. Offers from 27 [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] schools he knew almost nothing about rolled in."
With the help of his AAU coaches, Ezeli narrowed his list to [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]], [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]], [[Harvard Crimson men's basketball|Harvard]], and [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]]. The Vanderbilt coaching staff sold Ezeli on the school, citing its academic reputation and the program's recent experience with international players. Head coach [[Kevin Stallings]] added that Ezeli would be able to [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] his first year at the school to allow him more time to develop, since the program had a highly touted Australian prospect, [[Andrew Ogilvy|A.J. Ogilvy]], arriving at the same time and playing Ezeli's position. ==College career== Ezeli arrived in [[Nashville, Tennessee|Nashville]] in 2007 as a [[biology]] major and among the rawest of basketball prospects. During his first two years in the program, while still learning many of the basics of the sport, Ezeli was frequently dominated in practice by Ogilvy. However, as early as midway through his redshirt freshman season, the Commodores staff noticed that Ogilvy was beginning to have difficulty scoring against Ezeli in practice. While obsessively studying the game and working on his basic skills, Ezeli spent his first two seasons of eligibility primarily as a backup to Ogilvy, occasionally starting, until Ogilvy declared for the [[2010 NBA draft|NBA draft]] after the [[2009–10 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|2009–10 season]]. [[File:Festus Ezeli Vanderbilt Free Throw.jpg|thumb|right|Ezeli in 2012]] With Ogilvy gone, Ezeli had a breakout season in [[2010–11 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|2010–11]], averaging 13 points and 6.3 rebounds{{cite web|url=http://www.secdigitalnetwork.com/Portals/3/SEC%20Website/menshoops/CONFLDRS.HTM#conf.wki |title=Individual Basketball Statistics |work=2010–11 SEC Men's Basketball Statistics |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=April 2, 2011 |access-date=August 19, 2011}} while being named a second-team All-SEC ([[Southeastern Conference]]) performer.{{cite press release|url=http://www.secdigitalnetwork.com/NEWS/tabid/473/Article/222025/2011-sec-mens-hoops-awards-announced.aspx |title=2011 SEC Men's Hoops Awards Announced |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=March 8, 2011 |access-date=August 19, 2011}} He also broke [[Will Perdue]]'s Vanderbilt single-season record for [[block (basketball)|blocked shots]]. Ezeli's improvement was noted by many in the basketball world; then-[[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] coach [[Bruce Pearl]] told the ''Chattanooga Times Free Press'', "I don't think they miss [Ogilvy] at all. Ezeli has improved so much that he gives them the best of both worlds [offense and defense]." Before the [[2011–12 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|2011–12 season]], Ezeli was also named by ''Basketball Prospectus'' in its preseason outlook as one of the top 20 players in men's college basketball, along with teammates [[John Jenkins (basketball)|John Jenkins]] and [[Jeffery Taylor]].{{cite web|url=https://insider.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story?id=6836994 |title=CBB Summer Buzz: Vanderbilt |first=Elena |last=Bergeron |publisher=ESPN |date=August 9, 2011 |access-date=August 25, 2011}} (full article behind paywall; cited information in free preview) As the Commodores were preparing for Ezeli's final season at Vanderbilt, Stallings said about him:
"He now has a feel for the game. He has made himself an effective player. I think it's very rare. All of us are looking for more finished products. But we all understood if the payday came, if it really came, if he understood the game, if he was experienced, then it was going to give him a chance to be different than other guys. He didn't learn the game in elementary school like I did. He was trying to learn the game while competing effectively in the SEC. That makes it even more amazing."
==Professional career== ===Golden State Warriors (2012–2016)=== [[File:Festus Ezeli.jpg|thumb|right|Ezeli at practice in 2012]] Ezeli was selected by the [[Golden State Warriors]] with the 30th overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]]. On July 6, 2012, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Warriors.{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/ezeli_signed_070612 | title=Warriors Sign Festus Ezeli To Contract | work=NBA.com | date = July 6, 2012 | access-date = October 24, 2020}} As a rookie in [[2012-13 NBA season|2012–13]], Ezeli started many games for the Warriors in place of injured center [[Andrew Bogut]]. On January 19, 2013, Ezeli had a season-best game with 13 points and eight rebounds in 116–112 victory over the [[New Orleans Hornets]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400278316|title = Warriors vs. Hornets - Box Score - January 19, 2013 - ESPN}} In June 2013, Ezeli was ruled out for six to nine months after undergoing surgery on his right knee.[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/ezeli_rightknee_surgery_061313 Warriors Center Festus Ezeli Undergoes Successful Surgery on Right Knee] Ezeli subsequently missed the entire [[2013-14 NBA season|2013–14 season]]. Ezeli returned to action for the Warriors in the team's 2014–15 season opener. On December 22, 2014, he scored a then-career-high 15 points in a 128–108 victory over the [[Sacramento Kings]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400578707 Warriors dominate Kings in all facets as Klay Thompson leads way] The following day, Ezeli sprained his left ankle in a loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] and was confined to a moon boot.[http://www.warriorsworld.net/2014/12/27/warriors-news-festus-ezeli-will-wear-boot-to-protect-ankle/ Warriors News: Festus Ezeli Will Wear Boot To Protect Ankle] The injury kept him out all of January, when on January 28, 2015, Ezeli was assigned to the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA Development League]] for rehabilitation.[https://www.nba.com/warriors/warriors-assign-festus-ezeli-santa-cruz-recall-ognjen-kuzmic-d-league Warriors Assign Festus Ezeli to Santa Cruz; Recall Ognjen Kuzmic from D-League] On February 2, he was recalled by Golden State after successfully competing in two D-League games.[https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-recall-festus-ezeli-santa-cruz Warriors Recall Festus Ezeli From Santa Cruz] The following day, Ezeli made his return for Golden State, playing eight minutes of action in a 121–96 victory over the Kings. In the 2015 NBA playoffs, Ezeli logged key minutes as the first big man off the bench, often filling in for the foul-prone Andrew Bogut. The Warriors, with the help of Ezeli, advanced deep into the postseason to win the Western Conference Finals against [[James Harden]] and the [[Houston Rockets]] in five games. Ezeli won his first NBA championship after the Warriors defeated the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the [[2015 NBA Finals]] in six games.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/e/ezelife01/gamelog/2015/ Festus Ezeli 2014–15 Game Log] On August 1, 2015, Ezeli played for Team Africa at the [[NBA Africa Game 2015|2015 NBA Africa exhibition game]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13359599 NBA stars, legends shine as Team World rallies to beat Team Africa] On November 6, he scored a career-high 16 points as a starter in a 119–104 victory over the Denver Nuggets.[http://www.nba.com/games/20151106/DENGSW/gameinfo.html Warriors stay unbeaten behind another big night from Curry] The Warriors' NBA-record start ended after 24 wins when they lost to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] 108–95 on December 12.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151212/GSWMIL/gameinfo.html |title=It's over: Bucks hand Warriors 1st loss, win 108–95 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=December 13, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151212000353/http://www.nba.com/games/20151212/GSWMIL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 12, 2015 |url-status=dead }} On February 8, 2016, Ezeli underwent successful arthroscopic surgery to clean out debris from his left knee and was subsequently ruled out for six weeks.[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/festus-ezeli-surgery-20160208 Warriors Center Festus Ezeli Undergoes Successful Surgery] Ezeli returned to action on April 3 against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] after missing 31 games.[http://www.nba.com/games/20160403/PORGSW/gameinfo.html Warriors rebound from rare home loss to beat Blazers 136-111] Ezeli helped the Warriors win an NBA record 73 games to eclipse the 72 wins set by the [[1995–96 Chicago Bulls season|1995–96 Chicago Bulls]]. The Warriors made it to the [[2016 NBA Finals]] after overcoming a 3–1 deficit against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], winning the Western Conference Finals in seven games. However, the Warriors lost to the Cavaliers in seven games despite a 3–1 lead. === Portland Trail Blazers (2016–17) === On July 7, 2016, Ezeli signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].[http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-festus-ezeli TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN FESTUS EZELI] On August 23, he was ruled out for six weeks after undergoing a left knee injection.[http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-center-festus-ezeli-undergoes-injection-left-knee TRAIL BLAZERS CENTER FESTUS EZELI UNDERGOES INJECTION IN LEFT KNEE] Two months later, Ezeli suffered a minor setback in his comeback from the procedure, with swelling in his knee.{{Cite web |url=http://www.csnnw.com/portland-trail-blazers/trail-blazers-center-festus-ezeli-suffers-minor-setback-comeback |title=TRAIL BLAZERS' CENTER FESTUS EZELI SUFFERS MINOR SETBACK IN COMEBACK |access-date=November 9, 2016 |archive-date=November 10, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161110044213/http://www.csnnw.com/portland-trail-blazers/trail-blazers-center-festus-ezeli-suffers-minor-setback-comeback |url-status=dead }} In mid-December, it became apparent to the Trail Blazers that conservative treatment of Ezeli's aching left knee was not working, and that season-ending surgery was imminent.[http://www.nba.com/article/2016/12/17/report-portland-trailblazers-center-festus-ezeli-may-need-season-ending-surgery Report: Trail Blazers' Festus Ezeli may need season-ending surgery] On March 8, 2017, Ezeli underwent knee surgery and was ruled out for the rest of the [[2016-17 NBA season|2016–17 season]].[http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/ezeli-undergoes-knee-surgery EZELI UNDERGOES KNEE SURGERY] On June 30, 2017, Ezeli was waived by the Trail Blazers without having played a game for them.[http://www.csnbayarea.com/warriors/trail-blazers-waive-former-warriors-center-festus-ezeli TRAIL BLAZERS WAIVE FORMER WARRIORS CENTER FESTUS EZELI][http://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/nba-free-agency-blazers-waive-festus-ezeli-before-he-ever-plays-a-game-for-them/ NBA Free Agency: Blazers waive Festus Ezeli before he ever plays a game for them] === Westchester Knicks (2021) === On March 2, 2021, Ezeli signed a contract with the [[Westchester Knicks]] of the [[NBA G League]], returning to [[professional basketball]] after a four-year hiatus dealing with multiple injuries and difficult recoveries. He was immediately assigned the number 20 jersey.{{cite web|title=Knicks Acquire Festus Ezeli from Available Player Pool|url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/knicks-acquire-festus-ezeli-from-available-player-pool/|website=NBA.com|date=March 2, 2021|access-date=March 2, 2021}} Ezeli appeared in two games.{{cite news|title=Festus Ezeli signs with Rivers Hoopers in NBA/FIBA's Basketball Africa League|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/festus-ezeli-signs-with-rivers-hoopers-in-nba-fibas-basketball-africa-league/|newspaper=Sportando|date=April 17, 2021|access-date=April 17, 2021}} On April 17, 2021, Ezeli signed with [[Rivers Hoopers]] to play in the [[2021 BAL season|inaugural season]] of the [[Basketball Africa League]] (BAL). However, he did not play a game for the Hoopers before getting injured and being replaced by [[Robinson Opong]].{{cite news |title=Basketball: Rivers Hoopers sign Ugandan star to replace injured Ezeli |url=https://www.premiumtimesng.com/sports/nigeria-sports-news/456901-basketball-rivers-hoopers-sign-ugandan-star-to-replace-injured-ezeli.html |access-date=20 August 2021 |date=22 April Although Ezeli began his Vanderbilt studies as a biology major, he changed his major to economics because of the time demands of basketball. Vanderbilt chancellor [[Nicholas S. Zeppos|Nicholas Zeppos]] said of Ezeli: "You can imagine what it's like to hear his perspective on world trade, globalization and the economics of American sports." Ezeli's parents live in [[Sacramento]].{{cite news|last1=Faraudo|first1=Jeff|title=Festus Ezeli and the long, strange trip to the NBA|url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2015/05/24/festus-ezeli-and-the-long-strange-trip-to-the-nba|access-date=October 24, 2020|work=San Jose Mercury News|date=May 24, 2015}} Ezeli became an American citizen in September 2019.{{cite web |title=NBA Champion Festus Ezeli Returns to Nigeria to Reunite with Family, Give Back Through Basketball |url=https://closeup360.com/uncategorized/nba-champion-festus-ezeli-returns-nigeria-reunite-family-give-back-through-basketball/ |website=CloseUp360 |access-date=January 15, 2025 |date=December 31, 2019}} ==See also== *{{Portal-inline|Sports}} ==References== {{reflist|30em}} ==External links== {{commons}} {{basketballstats|nba=203105|bbr=e/ezelife01}} * [https://web.archive.org/web/20140502002515/http://www.vucommodores.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/ezeli_festus00.html Vanderbilt Commodores bio] {{Navboxes|list= {{2012 NBA draft}} {{Golden State Warriors 2014–15 NBA champions}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Ezeli, Festus}} [[Category:1989 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Golden State Warriors draft picks]] [[Category:Golden State Warriors players]] [[Category:Jesuit High School (Carmichael) alumni]] [[Category:NBA players from Nigeria]] [[Category:Nigerian expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Nigerian men's basketball players]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Yuba City, California]] [[Category:Santa Cruz Warriors players]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Benin City]] [[Category:Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball players]] [[Category:Yuba College alumni]]
